newsitem.title: USA: Italy's budget bill will bring rates down - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy's budget bill will bring rates down - Ciampi.

text.p: Italy's budget bill for 1997 is expected to help bring interest rates down, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi reaffirmed Saturday.
"We count on interest rates falling, even though we did not insert any savings (from an interest rate cut) in the bill," Ciampi, attending the IMF-World Bank annual meeting, told reporters.
"It will be a prize for our good behaviour, not something that we discount for from the start," Ciampi said.

Friday the Italian government passed a budget bill aimed at cutting the deficit by 60 trillion lire. The proposal, which will now have to be endorsed by Parliament, includes a 13 trillion lire "Euro tax" and 12 trillion in unspecified treasury operations. The remaining 37.5 trillion lire in deficit cuts will be effected through 25 trillion lire spending cuts and 12.5 trillion lire extra revenue.

Referring to the new heavy tax burden, Ciampi said he believed Italians with their desire to step into the single European currency from the start, will be able to take up the extra burden responsibly. "It's a big target, one that Italy has been pursuing for years". He said the "tax for Europe" will be a one-time imposition and will not be repeated.
